A rainy playtime

It is Friday. It is rainy today. Tom and May are not in the park. They are in the classroom. Tom has a puzzle. It is on a small table. May has some paper and three crayons. She draws a blue bird. Tom looks at her picture and smiles. Then May helps Tom with the puzzle. They put the puzzle and crayons away before class. Their teacher says, 'Thank you!'

originalGroup.material:
A call about Saturday art

Emma: Hello. Is the art room open on Saturday?
Mr Hill: Yes. It opens at ten and closes at twelve. We will paint paper boats at ten fifteen.
Emma: Do I need to bring a brush?
Mr Hill: No. We have brushes and paint here. Please bring an old shirt to wear.
Emma: Can my little brother come? He is five.
Mr Hill: The painting activity is for children from eight to eleven. Your brother can join the story club next door. That club is for children from five to seven.
Emma: How much is the painting activity?
Mr Hill: Three pounds. Please book a place by Friday.
Emma: Thank you. I'll ask my mum to book it.

originalGroup.material:
A small job for Bird

Rabbit and Goat wanted to make a reading seat beside the village tree. Rabbit drew a plan, and Goat carried the long pieces of wood. Bird flew down and asked, 'Can I help?'

Goat looked at Bird's little wings. 'The wood is heavy,' he said. Bird felt sad and sat on a branch. From there, she saw dark clouds coming towards the village.

'We must keep the wood dry!' she called. Rabbit and Goat were busy and did not look up. Bird flew to an empty shed and found its door open. She came back and showed them the way. They moved the wood into the shed just before the rain began.

The next day, they finished the seat. Goat asked Bird to choose a place for a small sign. She chose a spot where everyone on the path could see it. The sign said, 'Built by Rabbit, Goat and Bird.' Bird smiled. Her name was on it, although she had not carried one piece of wood.
